from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Framing the Linear System", [
            "Equations represent building a vector 'b' from v1, v2.",
            "Think of this like a robot arm reaching a target.",
            "Variables x1, x2 define our reach in each direction."
        ])
        
        # Setup vectors
        v1 = Vector([1, 1], color=BLUE)
        v2 = Vector([2, -0.5], color=BLUE)
        v_b = Vector([3, 1.5], color="#FF4500") # b
        
        # Labels
        l1 = MathTex("v_1", color=BLUE).next_to(v1.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        l2 = MathTex("v_2", color=BLUE).next_to(v2.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        lb = MathTex("b", color="#FF4500").next_to(v_b.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Present 2D linear system matrix A and vectors
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 4, 1], y_range=[-1, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'E6')
        
        # Start vectors at origin
        v1.shift(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        v2.shift(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        v_b.shift(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(v1), Create(l1), Create(v2), Create(l2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Robot arm reaching target
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        # Visualizing b as sum
        self.play(Create(v_b), Create(lb))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Variables x1, x2
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        x_label = MathTex("x_1v_1 + x_2v_2 = b", font_size=24).to_edge(DOWN)
        self.add(x_label)
        self.play(FadeIn(x_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Substitution (Cramer's Rule)", 
                          ["Replace v1 with 'b' to form a new shape.", 
                           "The area ratio tells us the scaling factor x1.", 
                           "This geometric substitution is the core of Cramer's Rule."])
        
        # Define vectors
        v1 = Vector([1, 2], color=BLUE)
        v2 = Vector([2, -1], color=YELLOW)
        b = Vector([1.5, 1], color="#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # Create shapes
        orig_shape = Polygon(ORIGIN, [1, 2, 0], [3, 1, 0], [2, -1, 0], color=WHITE)
        new_shape = Polygon(ORIGIN, [1.5, 1, 0], [3.5, 0, 0], [2, -1, 0], color="#FF4500")
        
        self.place_in_area(orig_shape, "A1", "C3")
        self.play(Create(orig_shape))
        
        self.place_in_area(new_shape, "D1", "F3")
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(orig_shape.copy(), new_shape))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        label = Text("Area(b, v2) / Area(v1, v2) = x1", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "B5")
        self.play(Write(label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#98FB98")
        box = SurroundingRectangle(self.lecture[2], color="#98FB98", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Compare the areas of the substituted versus original shapes.",
            "x1 is the ratio of these specific parallelogram areas.",
            "Cramer's Rule interprets linear systems as area scaling."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visual Synthesis and Conclusion", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        color_1 = "#FF9999" # Red-ish
        color_2 = "#99FF99" # Green-ish
        color_3 = "#9999FF" # Blue-ish

        # Setup parallelograms (visual gauge)
        rect_original = Polygon(ORIGIN, RIGHT*2, RIGHT*2+UP*2, UP*2, color=WHITE)
        rect_sub = Polygon(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5, RIGHT*1.5+UP*2.5, UP*2.5, color=color_1)
        
        group = VGroup(rect_original, rect_sub).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(group, 'A2', 'D5')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        label_ratio = MathTex(r"x_1 = \frac{\text{Area}(A_1)}{\text{Area}(A)}", color=color_2)
        self.place_at_grid(label_ratio, 'E3')
        
        self.play(Write(label_ratio))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        label_cramer = Text("Cramer's Rule: Geometric Scaling", color=color_3, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_cramer, 'F3')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(label_cramer))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_3)
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(group), FadeOut(label_ratio), FadeOut(label_cramer))

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Area Interpretation of Determinants
sections.content: Briefly explain that the determinant of a 2x2 matrix represents the signed area of the parallelogram formed by the column vectors. Introduce the visual concept of scaling space.
sections.example: Visualizing a square defined by vectors (1,0) and (0,1) transforming into a skewed parallelogram with area |det(A)|.

sections.title: Framing the Linear System
sections.content: Represent the system Ax = b as a vector equation: x1*v1 + x2*v2 = b. Explain that solving for x1 and x2 means finding how much of vector v1 and vector v2 we need to reach the 'target' b.
sections.example: A robot arm with two segments (v1, v2) trying to reach a target point 'b' in a 2D plane.

sections.title: Geometric Substitution (The Cramer's Rule Logic)
sections.content: Show that replacing one column of the matrix with the vector 'b' creates a new parallelogram. Explain that the ratio of the area of this new parallelogram to the original is exactly the scalar value of x1.
sections.example: Swapping v1 with the target vector 'b' creates a new shape. If the area of this new shape is double the original, then x1 must be 2.

sections.title: Visual Synthesis and Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize that Cramer's Rule is simply comparing 'areas'. Highlight that x1 = det(A1)/det(A) and x2 = det(A2)/det(A) provides a global view of scaling transformation.
sections.example: A 'Scaling Gauge' animation showing the original unit parallelogram vs. the Cramer-substituted parallelograms as the system solves for 'b'.
